newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CABINET REFORM SEEN DELAYING HANDLOWY OFFER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CABINET REFORM SEEN DELAYING HANDLOWY OFFER.

text.p: Poland's government reform, under which key economic ministries have been merged or replaced by new ones, is delaying a tender for an adviser in the privatisation of Bank Handlowy SA, a government official said.
The finance ministry had planned to announce a tender by the end of 1996 for a firm that would advise it in the bank's sell-off, which is planned for this year.

But the official, who declined to be named, said on Tuesday uncertainty over which ministry would oversee the privatisation put off the tender announcement even though the cabinet approved the Handlowy privatisation plan early in December.
"There is a question of who will implement the Handlowy privatisation plan after the government reform," he said.

He said the government approved the finance ministry's blueprint which envisaged selling a 30 percent stake in Bank Handlowy to strategic investors, following this with a 30-percent public offering and setting aside 30 percent of shares for yet-to-be created pension funds.
Five-percent stakes would be reserved for Handlowy employees and a planned special fund to compensate owners of property confiscated under communism.

The government late last month approved regulations defining areas of competence of particular ministries but they have yet to be published to come into force and it is unclear whether the Handlowy sale should be handled by the finance or the treasury ministry.

Under the government reform a privatisation ministry was integrated last October into a new, more powerful treasury ministry and from January 1 a new ministry of economy replaced the industry and foreign trade ministries.
